<p>After arriving at the headquarters early in the morning, I was told to wait once the Association member finished verifying my identity. As I sat and waited, another Association member came and guided me deep into the basement on the 7th floor.</p><p>‘There’s a 7th floor underground?’</p><p>It had everything—showers, training grounds, even a cafeteria. It felt less like a workspace and more like an underground bunker.</p><p>A perfect place to plan and prepare for covert operations.</p><p>Past the door in the corner of the Association building, there were three more security-locked doors before reaching the elevator. They said you could only get here by taking that elevator.</p><p>There was a joke on Hunter Gallery that the Association’s basement had a torture chamber. Seeing this place, I was half-convinced there might not be a torture room, but there was definitely a floor where they secretly detained and interrogated criminals without the state’s knowledge.</p><p>The conference room was noisy. Over 30 Hunters from the Association were gathered inside.</p><p>Among them, about seven were well-known Hunters whose names any Hunter would recognize.</p><p>‘Where’s Hye-na?’</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>I turned my head when I felt someone familiar behind me—it was Min Se-rin. Our eyes met, but she just gave a slight nod before looking away.</p><p>Everyone else seemed to know each other, laughing and chatting away.</p><p>‘I’m the only one left out…’</p><p>It reminded me of my trainee days, when everyone else was happy, eating and talking together—except me.</p><p>‘Fuck…’</p><p>Just then, the door behind the podium opened, and Hye-na stepped out, dressed in a formal suit.</p><p>The noisy room fell silent as all eyes turned to her.</p><p>Hye-na scanned the room, and when her gaze met mine, she gave a small smile before stepping up to the microphone.</p><p>“Ah, a—can everyone hear me? I’m Kang Hye-na, the director in charge of this operation.”</p><p>Most seemed to be listening, but a few were openly sleeping or goofing off.</p><p>“Then…”</p><p>At Hye-na’s signal, the lights dimmed, the screen lowered, and the beam projector turned on.</p><p>“Th-then, I’ll begin the briefing.”</p><p>Just then, one Hunter raised his hand high, as if he had a question.</p><p>“Yes? Hunter Lee Seung-jun, do you have a question?”</p><p>“Yes, will Director Kang be the one explaining the operation?”</p><p>A few snickers spread through the room at Lee Seung-jun’s question.</p><p>“Is there a problem?”</p><p>Hye-na answered with a bright smile, but her lips were trembling slightly.</p><p>That was her slightly pissed-off look.</p><p>“It’s not a problem, per se… but Director Kang, you’re not exactly good at explaining things like this… There’s an Association member here who specializes in briefings, so why are you doing it yourself?”</p><p>“What?!”</p><p>Hye-na flared up, and the Hunters in the conference room began to murmur.</p><p>“Director Kang has a thing for stuff like this, doesn’t she?”</p><p>“Seung-kacol… He actually said that to her face…”</p><p>“As expected of Dae Seung-jun. He says what needs to be said.”</p><p>“She even has staff assigned to handle paperwork and her weaker areas since the Association President arranged it for her, so why does she always insist on doing everything herself?”</p><p>“But she works hard, though~.”</p><p>Hye-na crumpled the paper in her hand, her fingers trembling as she glared at Seung-jun.</p><p>“Seung-jun… youuu!”</p><p>Seung-jun quickly lowered his hand, crossed his arms, and closed his eyes.</p><p>Just then, the woman who looked like a secretary standing next to Hye-na approached her.</p><p>‘Ah, she’s the one who was with Hye-na when Na-hyeon moved into the official residence.’</p><p>The secretary whispered a few words into Hye-na’s ear, and after shooting Seung-jun one last glare, Hye-na stepped down from the podium.</p><p>“We will now begin the operation briefing. Hunter Seung-jun, you will have a separate meeting with the Director after the explanation.”</p><p>The surrounding Hunters snickered, and Seung-jun let out a sigh.</p><p>After that, the secretary took over and began the operation briefing.</p><p>‘Is this a sitcom?’</p><p>***</p><p>The operation briefing was shocking.</p><p>It wasn’t just a simple criminal organization. On the surface, it began as an ordinary retired Hunter club composed of former Hunters.</p><p>Outwardly, it appeared to be a wholesome retired Hunter club focused on volunteer work, but in reality, most of its members were Hunters who had either been dismissed after severe disciplinary action from the Association or had resigned when the Association began internal investigations due to their shady backgrounds.</p><p>The Association had long suspected this club and had obtained detailed information through an informant.</p><p>In truth, it was a criminal organization engaged in human trafficking, organ trafficking, drug manufacturing, and distribution—every kind of crime imaginable.</p><p>According to the informant’s expose, the club was just a front, and the real operation was an illegal business run by a construction company called Baekgwang Construction.</p><p>‘Baekgwang Construction…’</p><p>It was a company founded by Baek Gwang-hyeon, an A-rank Hunter who had made a name for himself exploring countless Gates during the global Gate outbreak, after he left the Association.</p><p>Even as a trainee, I had heard the name Baek Gwang-hyeon—he was a legendary Hunter.</p><p>Baek Gwang-hyeon had left the Association after conflicts with high-ranking officials, retired as a Hunter, and started a construction company. But in reality, it was a criminal organization involved in trafficking organs and drugs to China and Southeast Asia.</p><p>It wasn’t just organ trafficking—there were reports that they kidnapped young Awakened and sold their organs.</p><p>In places like China, there were rumors of underground surgeries where receiving an Awakened’s organ could turn someone into an Awakened.</p><p>Even if a normal person receives an Awakened’s organ transplant, they won’t become an Awakened. In fact, it’s common sense for normal people to receive organs from other normal people.</p><p>If a normal person receives an Awakened’s organ, modern medicine can’t predict the countless side effects that would follow.</p><p>Even for blood transfusions, the blood of normal people and Awakened is strictly separated.</p><p>But recently, there’s a rumor circulating within China that if you use a special transplant surgery with drugs made from materials obtained from Gates, normal people can become Awakened.</p><p>The Hunter Association can’t confirm the truth of this rumor, but for criminals, the truth doesn’t matter.</p><p>What matters to them is that Chinese tycoons are trading Awakened organs at astronomical prices.</p><p>Surprisingly, China’s control over Awakened is far stricter than in South Korea, so they can’t operate within China. Instead, they’ve turned their eyes to Southeast Asia, Korea, and Japan.</p><p>The location we’ll be raiding in this operation is a building in the mountains. According to an insider, young Awakened children are being held captive there. They’re either dissected or sold alive to China.</p><p>Our mission is to arrest the key executives and collect evidence.</p><p>Once the evidence is gathered, the Intelligence Investigation Bureau will take over, publicize the truth nationwide, and arrest Baek Gwang-hyeon.</p><p>There’s a major deal happening next week, so most of the executives and children will be gathered at that building. That’s when we’ll strike.</p><p>The second issue is drugs.</p><p>There’s intelligence that Baek Gwang Construction is manufacturing and distributing a drug called “Red Dust” overseas. It’s a red powder made by synthesizing various materials from Gates.</p><p>Red Dust is known as the king of drugs, the “dream drug.” Inhaling it once is said to give you heightened senses and a taste of what true paradise feels like.</p><p>Of course, it’s highly addictive, and no country in the world legalizes it.</p><p>And yet, it’s being produced in Korea.</p><p>Through these crimes, Baek Gwang-hyeon is said to have amassed a fortune exceeding tens of trillions of won last year.</p><p>‘Fuck… is this really South Korea?’</p><p>***</p><p>After the briefing, we were each assigned our own rooms.</p><p>Starting tomorrow, we’ll spend four days here, repeating operation drills before being deployed.</p><p>Late at night, I sit alone in the dining hall, thinking about the operation.</p><p>Naturally, all external communications have been cut off. There might be a mole inside.</p><p>Actually, if you think about it, there has to be a mole somewhere in the Association.</p><p>Without the cooperation of high-ranking Association officials, it would be impossible to carry out such atrocious crimes for over a year while evading the Association’s watch.</p><p>At first, I had doubts about an operation where murder could happen, but after hearing the explanation, I feel like it’d be fine to just kill all of them.</p><p>Instead of using taxpayer money to lock them up in an Awakened prison and feed them, it’d be better for society to just capture the key figures, extract confessions, and execute the rest on the spot.</p><p>‘And once the trial’s over for the important ones, we can just carry out the death sentence immediately…’</p><p>My conflicted heart felt a little lighter.</p><p>‘I wouldn’t feel guilty even if they died by accident.’</p><p>I let out a deep sigh and stood up from my chair to head back to my room when the cafeteria door opened.</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“Ah.”</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="290675" loading="lazy">
</p><p>Standing at the door was Min Se-rin. She still had that sharp look about her.</p><p>“Ah, hello.”</p><p>“Yes, hello.”</p><p>We exchanged awkward greetings, and just as I was about to leave the cafeteria, Min Se-rin stopped me.</p><p>“Um…”</p><p>“Yes?”</p><p>“Were you doing something in the cafeteria?”</p><p>“Huh? I was just… sitting there.”</p><p>What was she getting at? Did she think I was making contact with someone outside?</p><p>Min Se-rin was staring at me with deep suspicion.</p><p>“Just sitting there…?”</p><p>“Yeah… I had some things to think about… Wait, why are you asking?”</p><p>Min Se-rin looked at me, then averted her gaze, her voice tinged with a hint of embarrassment.</p><p>“Ah… well… I… I came because I was hungry, and I thought maybe if you were eating something… maybe… no, if it’s inconvenient, I wasn’t trying to suggest we eat together…”</p><p>“Ah…”</p><p>Min Se-rin’s face was flushed red, completely at odds with her sharp appearance, and she was babbling nervously, as if she didn’t even know what she was saying.</p><p>Her outward appearance was like a mix of Chae Ryu-ah and Yoon Ji-hyeon.</p><p>‘Prejudice is a scary thing.’</p><p>Despite her sharp look, the way she was flustered in front of me right now made her seem a little… foolish.</p><p>‘Last time I saw her, her tone and demeanor seemed cold… but anyway, I am a bit hungry.’</p><p>“Then…”</p><p>“Ah, yes. I guess I’ll have to hold out until morning.”</p><p>“No, how about we look for some ramen? The cafeteria is so big, there’s bound to be something…”</p><p>Min Se-rin’s expression brightened instantly.</p><p>“Yes! Then I’ll check the left side first!”</p>
